# Radisson Joins ChatGPT: What This New Hotel Plugin Means for Travelers

> **In short:** Radisson Hotel Group has teamed up with Accenture to build a ChatGPT plugin that helps travelers find, compare, and book hotels while planning their trips, using OpenAI's technology. It signals a growing shift toward planning whole trips inside an AI chat window.

Planning a trip usually means jumping between five tabs: a search engine, a hotel site, a map, reviews, and your notes app. Radisson is betting that one of those tabs can go away.

According to the company's announcement, Radisson Hotel Group has partnered with Accenture (a large consulting and tech firm) to build a ChatGPT plugin, an add-on that lets ChatGPT pull live information and actions from another service. Built on OpenAI's technology, the plugin is designed to help travelers find, compare, and book Radisson hotels while they plan a trip, all inside a single conversation with the AI.

## How a ChatGPT plugin actually works

A plugin is a small bridge between ChatGPT and another company's system. When you turn one on, ChatGPT can ask that company's servers for real, up-to-date information, or even complete a task like starting a booking, instead of just guessing based on what it learned during training.

For a hotel plugin, that could mean the AI checks actual room availability, prices, and locations straight from Radisson's own system, rather than making recommendations based on old or general knowledge. Think of it like the difference between asking a friend who *thinks* they remember a hotel chain, and asking one who is on the phone with the front desk.

## Why a hotel group would do this

Trip planning is one of the most-searched activities on the internet, and the search usually starts in a chat-style tool these days. By meeting travelers inside ChatGPT, Radisson can show up earlier in the process, when a person types something like *"I need a hotel in Lisbon for a long weekend in October."*

Accenture's role, according to the announcement, is the technical and design work that ties Radisson's booking system into the AI experience. The companies frame it as a way to make hotel discovery feel more like a conversation and less like filling out filters.

## What this means for you

- **If you're planning a trip:** Keep an eye on the ChatGPT plugin store. If the Radisson plugin is available in your account, you'll be able to describe what you want (city, dates, vibe) and have the AI pull real Radisson options. You still confirm the booking yourself, the AI is doing the searching, not signing on your behalf without your click.
- **If you already use ChatGPT for travel ideas:** This is a step toward fewer copy-paste hops between AI and booking sites. Today you might ask ChatGPT for a hotel shortlist, then go check each one. A plugin aims to fold those steps together.
- **If you've never used ChatGPT:** You don't need to do anything yet. This kind of feature is part of a slow rollout, and Radisson has not yet announced exactly when or where the plugin will be available, or whether it works in every country. Check the official ChatGPT plugin directory and Radisson's site for the latest.
- **If you already use it:** Once the plugin is live, you can layer it onto complex trip requests — like asking ChatGPT to compare a family-friendly Radisson in one city against a business-traveler-friendly one in another, with your dates and budget as constraints. The plugin lets the AI do the side-by-side math instead of you.

## Wrap-up

Radisson's move with Accenture is a small but telling example of how everyday tasks, including booking a hotel, are starting to move into AI chat windows. If trip planning is something you do even a couple of times a year, try opening ChatGPT next time and see what's already available for travel. The tools are catching up to the way you already think through a trip.
